name: Avocados
description: Creamy, mellow, and worth catching at just the right moment. A little give tells you more than color alone.

storage.label: Ripe
storage.preparation: Keep whole until you need it.
storage.advice: Once the fruit yields gently in your palm, move it to the fridge to slow further ripening.
storage.caution: Firm avocado? Let it ripen on the counter first.

storage.label: Unripe
storage.preparation: Place in a paper bag to encourage ripening.
storage.advice: Check daily for a little give under gentle pressure, then refrigerate.
storage.caution: Avoid squeezing with your fingertips; that can bruise the flesh.

storage.label: Cut
storage.preparation: Cover the exposed flesh and refrigerate.
storage.advice: Wash the outside before cutting. Keep the cut fruit covered in a clean container.
storage.caution: A color change is not a reliable safety test.

buying: For today, choose fruit that gives a little under gentle palm pressure.
For later in the week, choose a firmer avocado.
freshness: Avoid damaged fruit. Discard any that looks rotten; do not use appearance alone to judge safety.
leftovers: Spread on toast with cracked pepper.
tips: Check ripeness in your palm to avoid bruising.

freezing.instructions: For the tested purée method, peel and mash ripe flesh with 1 tablespoon lemon juice per 2 avocados. Pack with ½ inch headspace, seal, and freeze.
freezing.quality: Best used as a purée or spread after thawing.
